items.title: Reduce dependency tree to make Debian packaging feasible
items.body:
## Problem

The dependency tree of the `keystone` binary is very large, which makes building a proper Debian package problematic: many crates have no `librust-*-dev` package.

Measured on the default-feature build of `openstack-keystone` (normal dependencies, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `Cargo.lock` of the `raft` branch):

- 693 third-party crates in total.
- 144 have no Debian `-dev` package (checked against the Ubuntu 26.04 archive; recheck against the actual target, e.g. trixie/sid, since coverage differs).
- A further group is packaged only at an older, incompatible major version (see "Version skew").

Presence was checked by crate name only, so the real number of blockers is higher once semver is considered.

## Largest contributors

"Crates removed" counts crates that would leave the tree if the dependency were dropped.

| Dependency | Crates removed | Avoidable? |
|---|---|---|
| `extism` (WASM auth plugins, via `auth-plugin-runtime`) | 76 (wasmtime/cranelift tree) | Yes. Not feature-gated: `core` and `keystone` depend on `openstack-keystone-auth-plugin-runtime` unconditionally. |
| `sea-orm` | 26 | No, SQL core. |
| `fjall` + `openraft` | 27 | No for now (raft storage; both also tracked in #1304 as exempted/alpha). |
| `webauthn-rs` | 9 | Yes, `crates/webauthn` could be an optional feature. |
| `validator` | 7 | Partly (derive validation in `config`/`api-types`). |
| `governor` (+ `quanta`, `spinning_top`, `nonzero_ext`) | 6 | Partly, a small in-house token bucket would do. |
| `vaultrs` (`oslo-config` feature `vault`, on by default) | 5 | Yes, make `vault` default-off. |
| `utoipa` family (+ `yaml_serde`, `libyaml-rs`, swagger-ui `vendored`) | ~8 | Partly (swagger UI is the avoidable part). |
| `icu_*` (via `idna_adapter`) | 9 | Yes, use the unicode-rs backend of `idna_adapter`. |
| `aws-lc-rs` / `aws-lc-sys` | 2 | Yes. Debian has `ring` but no `aws-lc`. Switch `rustls`, `reqwest`, `ldap3`, `spiffe-rustls`, `rcgen` to the `ring` provider. |
| `spiffe*` | 3 | Probably not (raft mTLS identity). |
| `opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk` | 2 | Only if `telemetry` stops depending on them unconditionally (the `otel` feature exists, but these two are always compiled). |

### What-if

| Removed | Missing crates | Tree size |
|---|---|---|
| nothing | 144 | 693 |
| `extism` | 102 | 598 |
| `extism`, `vaultrs` | 99 | 593 |
| `extism`, `vaultrs`, `governor`, `validator`, `utoipa-swagger-ui`, `webauthn-rs`, `spiffe*` | 84 | 562 |

## Version skew

Packaged in Debian, but at an older major than the lock file requires:

| Crate | Locked | Debian |
|---|---|---|
| `rand` | 0.10 | 0.8 |
| `aes-gcm` | 0.11 | 0.10 |
| `argon2` | 0.6 | 0.5 |
| `jsonwebtoken` | 11 | 9 |
| `reqwest` | 0.13 | 0.12 |
| `prost` | 0.14 | 0.12 |
| `tonic` | 0.14 | 0.12 |
| `mockall` | 0.15 | 0.13 |
| `p256` | 0.14 | 0.13 |

The newest RustCrypto generation (`ctutils`, `cmov`, `hybrid-array`, `cpubits`, `phc`, `primefield`, `wnaf`) also pulls in crates Debian does not have. Pinning to previous majors would make that group packageable, but each needs an API compatibility check.

## Proposed work, in order of payoff

1. Feature-gate `extism` / `auth-plugin-runtime`, default-off. (~45 fewer crates to package, the hardest tree.)
2. Make `oslo-config`'s `vault` feature default-off; gate `webauthn`.
3. Switch the TLS crypto provider from `aws-lc` to `ring`.
4. Replace `governor` with an in-house limiter; drop `utoipa-swagger-ui` `vendored`.
5. Pin RustCrypto, `rand`, `reqwest` to Debian-packaged majors where the API difference is small.
6. Leave `sea-orm`, `openraft`, `fjall` for a separate packaging effort.

## Notes

- Related: #1304 (supply-chain / deployment validation).
- Analysis only; no code changed. Method: `cargo metadata --filter-platform x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, closure over normal dependencies from `openstack-keystone`, compared to `apt-cache dumpavail` `librust-*-dev` entries.

items.title: ARCH statement and keyfile location in DEB repo.
items.body:
### This issue is unique.

- [x] I have used the [search tool](https://github.com/Euro-Office/DesktopEditors/issues?q=) and did not find an issue describing my bug.

### Operating System

Linux

### Architecture

x86_64

### Package Type

deb

### Version information

9.3.6.0 (x64 deb) · build 2026-10-22

### Expected Behavior

The location for the apt repo keys given in the EO web at:

`https://euro-office.github.io/documentation/installation/`

The repo key commend locates the keyfile in:

`/etc/apt/keyrings/nextcloud-office.asc`

This is no longer supported in Mint 22.3 and leads to an error message on entering `sudo apt update`

Aldo, config does not state correct arch value, leading to the information statement below:

```
Fetched 249 kB in 3s (88.5 kB/s)           
Reading package lists... Done
Building dependency tree... Done
Reading state information... Done
All packages are up-to-date.
N: Skipping acquisition of configured file 'main/binary-i386/Packages', as repository 'https://download.nextcloud.com/office/repo/deb stable InRelease' doesn't support architecture 'i386'
```




### Actual Behavior

Error message stating that the storage of keys in /etc/apt/keyrings is no longer supported and lack of support for i386 architecture in Linux Mint 22.3

### Reproduction Steps

Run command for downloading of keys as advised:

```
sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
sudo curl -fsSL https://download.nextcloud.com/office/repo/nextcloud-office.asc \ -o /etc/apt/keyrings/nextcloud-office.asc
echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/nextcloud-office.asc] https://download.nextcloud.com/office/repo/deb stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nextcloud-office.list
```

run `sudo apt update`

You will get an error message sating that the storage of keys in subdirectory  /etc/apt is no longe supported and the repo update was ignored.

### Additional information

The resolution is to change the command to locate the keyfile in /usr/share/keyrings and edit the deb command to reflect this:

```
sudo curl -fsSL https://download.nextcloud.com/office/repo/nextcloud-office.asc -o /usr/share/keyrings/nextcloud-office.asc \
echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/nextcloud-office.asc] https://download.nextcloud.com/office/repo/deb stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nextcloud-office.list
```

The error message concerning the lack of support for i386 is not resolved by placing [arch=amd64] in the deb command i.e:
`
 "deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/nextcloud-office.asc] https://download.nextcloud.com/office/repo/deb stable main" `

items.title: setup.sh exits silently on non-Debian Linux: Tizen package manager requires dpkg/apt prereqs
items.body:
## What happens
On a non-Debian Linux (Arch here), `./scripts/setup.sh` prints `Installing Samsung TV extensions (a few minutes)…` and exits with no error.

## Cause
Before installing, Tizen's `package-manager-cli.bin` checks for host prerequisites with `dpkg -l <pkg> | grep ^ii` (in `PrerequisitesUtil`), then tries to `apt install` anything missing:
```
Failed to install the following packages automatically. Try to install them manually.
libkf5itemmodels5
libkf5kiowidgets5
libkchart2
rpm2cpio
cpio
```
Without `dpkg`, every check fails. The dependency tree of `TV-SAMSUNG-Public-WebAppDevelopment` and `Certificate-Manager` pulls in `heaptrack-prerequisites` and `dynamic-analyzer-product`, so both packages are refused. The command's output goes to `/dev/null` and `set -e` exits, so nothing tells you why.

`cert-add-on` and `TV-SAMSUNG-Extension-Tools` install fine.

## The two blocked packages aren't needed
`setup.sh` and `deploy.sh` only use `tizen certificate`, `security-profiles`, `package`, `install`, `run` and `sdb`. Those all come with the base web CLI. After I deleted the `"$PM" install` line, setup and deploy both worked and the app installed and ran on the TV.

## Possible fix
- Trim `PACKAGES` to what the scripts actually need (`cert-add-on TV-SAMSUNG-Extension-Tools`, or possibly none), and/or
- Don't send the package manager's output to `/dev/null`, or print it on failure, so the error is visible.

**Environment:** Arch-based Linux (Omarchy), Tizen Studio 6.1 web-cli, package manager 0.5.67

items.title: Install on Ubuntu with apt from a repository of our own
items.body:
### Why

On Ubuntu the formatter is a download from the release page that goes onto the `PATH` by hand, and nothing says when a new version is out. Ubuntu users expect `apt install` and `apt upgrade`. google-java-format was asked for the same in google/google-java-format#231; its maintainers did not take it on and offered to link a package made by someone else.

### Proposal

`.deb` packages for amd64 and arm64, made from the release's `open-java-format-linux-glibc_x86-64` and `open-java-format-linux-glibc_aarch64` and installing `/usr/bin/open-java-format`, in a signed apt repository of our own:

```sh
sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
curl -fsSL https://apt.openjavaformat.dev/key.asc | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/open-java-format.asc > /dev/null
echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/open-java-format.asc] https://apt.openjavaformat.dev stable main" \
  | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/open-java-format.list
sudo apt update
sudo apt install open-java-format
```

From then on `apt upgrade` brings every release. The same lines work on Debian.

How it could work, in the shape of the Homebrew tap in #151:

- A repository, `openjavaformat/apt`, published with GitHub Pages under `apt.openjavaformat.dev`.
- An hourly workflow follows the latest release. It downloads the two Linux binaries, checks them against `checksums_sha256.txt`, builds the two packages with `dpkg-deb`, writes the indexes with `apt-ftparchive`, signs `InRelease` and `Release.gpg`, and deploys the result as a Pages artifact, so no binary lands in Git history.
- The repository carries the latest version only. Older versions stay on the release page as plain binaries.

### To decide

- **The oldest supported release.** The Linux binaries are built on `ubuntu-latest`, today Ubuntu 24.04, and on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, both with glibc 2.39. A program linked against glibc 2.34 or later needs at least 2.34 to run: that is the "GLIBC_2.34 not found" of google/google-java-format#1072, which google-java-format fixed by building on an older image. Read the real minimum off our binaries with `objdump -T` and declare it as `Depends: libc6 (>= …)`. Ubuntu 22.04 has glibc 2.35 and Debian 12 has 2.36; Ubuntu 20.04 has 2.31 and is past its standard support. When `ubuntu-latest` moves to the next LTS, the minimum moves with it, so `release.yml` should name the image.
- **The signing key.** The key that signs the release files, or one of its own for the repository, which keeps the release key out of another repository's secrets.
- **Hosting.** A GitHub Pages site may be up to 1 GB and has a soft limit of 100 GB of traffic a month. Two packages of one version are far below the first; the second matters only if apt becomes the main way to install.

### Alternatives looked at

- **A PPA on Launchpad.** Launchpad builds every package from a source upload, without network access. GraalVM is not in the Ubuntu archive, so the prebuilt binary would have to travel inside the source package, and a PPA serves Ubuntu only.
- **Snap.** The Snap Store comes with Ubuntu and updates by itself, but a strictly confined snap sees only non-hidden files in the home directory and gets a `/tmp` of its own, so it could not format a checkout in `/workspace` or in a hidden directory. Classic confinement lifts that only after a manual review by the store.
- **The Ubuntu and Debian archives.** A package there must build from source inside the distribution, against dependencies packaged there too. GraalVM is not packaged, and the jar would bring the formatter's whole dependency tree along. Out of reach for now.
- **`.deb` files on the release page alone.** `sudo apt install ./open-java-format_<version>_amd64.deb` would work, but nothing would bring updates.
- **Homebrew on Linux.** The formula of #151 covers Ubuntu users who already use Homebrew.

### Done when

- `sudo apt install open-java-format` installs the latest release on amd64 and arm64, on every supported Ubuntu LTS release from the oldest one decided above, and `open-java-format --version` prints it;
- `apt upgrade` sees a new release within the hour, without a hand edit;
- the [Command line](https://openjavaformat.dev/get-started/command-line/) page gets an apt section, and [About](https://openjavaformat.dev/about/#where-it-is-published) lists the repository.

### Related

- google/google-java-format#231 and google/google-java-format#1072
- #151 for Homebrew, #152 for Windows

items.body:
## Problem
Nothing in this repo checks the licenses of its own dependencies (pip packages in `docker/grading-api/requirements*.txt`, apt packages in every Dockerfile, the upstream base images themselves). Confirmed via `grep -rln "pip-licenses\|license-checker\|licensed\b" scripts/ .github/` -- zero hits. Notable given how carefully this project scrutinized Kasm Workspaces Community Edition's own license (EULA §2.2, CLAUDE.md's own hard rule) before building around it -- the same rigor has never been applied to this project's own dependency tree.

## Fix
Add a license-scan step to `scripts/security-scan.sh` (e.g. `pip-licenses` for the Python deps, `licensecheck`/manual apt-package license review for system packages) with an explicit allow-list of acceptable licenses (MIT/BSD/Apache-2.0/etc.) and a deny-list for anything copyleft-incompatible with however this project is ultimately distributed/deployed. Decide the actual allow/deny policy first (a real judgment call, not something to guess at) before wiring in a hard CI gate.

## Source
Found during a Definition-of-Done architecture review requested by the user (2026-09-28).

items.title: CI: git-annex apt install wastes minutes per run in three jobs
items.body:
Owner observation during the v0.9.8 release: a required check spent ~17 minutes dominated by `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y git-annex`. Three jobs in `.github/workflows/test.yml` (around lines 118, 181, 344) repeat this on every run; `apt-get update` alone hits all mirrors, and git-annex's Haskell dependency tree is hundreds of MB.

Options, roughly in order of payoff:

- [ ] Audit which jobs actually exercise git-annex. If a tier (e.g. unit-pure) never shells out to it, drop the install there entirely — the classifier already content-greps tests, so the install list should match reality.
- [ ] Replace apt with the upstream standalone tarball: `curl -sL https://downloads.kitenet.net/git-annex/linux/current/git-annex-standalone-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz` + add to PATH — seconds instead of minutes, no apt update needed.
- [ ] Wrap it in `actions/cache` (or `awalsh128/cache-apt-pkgs-action`) keyed on the git-annex version so even the download amortizes.
- [ ] Skip `apt-get update` where apt stays (the runner images ship fresh indexes; a pinned install rarely needs it).

Same pattern likely exists in nightly-tests.yml — check while in there.

items.body:
My configuration management system detected that the way your buildkite-agent packages are built for Debian-based systems is not to spec, and prevents the full purging of packages, as per the following demonstration:

```
$ sudo apt install buildkite-agent
Reading package lists... Done
Building dependency tree       
Reading state information... Done
The following NEW packages will be installed:
  buildkite-agent
0 to upgrade, 1 to newly install, 0 to remove and 0 not to upgrade.
Need to get 0 B/12.3 MB of archives.
After this operation, 34.9 MB of additional disk space will be used.
Selecting previously unselected package buildkite-agent.
(Reading database ... 82096 files and directories currently installed.)
Preparing to unpack .../buildkite-agent_3.18.0-3219_amd64.deb ...
Unpacking buildkite-agent (3.18.0-3219) ...
Setting up buildkite-agent (3.18.0-3219) ...
 _           _ _     _ _    _ _                                _
| |         (_) |   | | |  (_) |                              | |
| |__  _   _ _| | __| | | ___| |_ ___    __ _  __ _  ___ _ __ | |_
| '_ \| | | | | |/ _` | |/ / | __/ _ \  / _` |/ _` |/ _ \ '_ \| __|
| |_) | |_| | | | (_| |   <| | ||  __/ | (_| | (_| |  __/ | | | |_
|_.__/ \__,_|_|_|\__,_|_|\_\_|\__\___|  \__,_|\__, |\___|_| |_|\__|
                                               __/ |
                                              |___/

You now need to add your agent token to "/etc/buildkite-agent/buildkite-agent.cfg"
and then you can start your agent by running "sudo systemctl enable buildkite-agent && sudo systemctl start buildkite-agent"
$ sudo apt purge buildkite-agent
Reading package lists... Done
Building dependency tree       
Reading state information... Done
The following packages will be REMOVED:
  buildkite-agent*
0 to upgrade, 0 to newly install, 1 to remove and 0 not to upgrade.
After this operation, 34.9 MB disk space will be freed.
Do you want to continue? [Y/n] 
(Reading database ... 82119 files and directories currently installed.)
Removing buildkite-agent (3.18.0-3219) ...
Stopping buildkite-agent systemd service
Purging configuration files for buildkite-agent (3.18.0-3219) ...
$ ls -la /etc/buildkite-agent/
total 16
drwxr-xr-x   3 buildkite-agent buildkite-agent 4096 Jan 29 17:19 .
drwxr-xr-x 102 root            root            4096 Jan 29 17:19 ..
-rw-------   1 buildkite-agent buildkite-agent 1734 Jan 29 17:19 buildkite-agent.cfg
drwxr-xr-x   2 buildkite-agent buildkite-agent 4096 Jan 29 17:19 hooks
$ dpkg -S /etc/buildkite-agent/buildkite-agent.cfg 
dpkg-query: no path found matching pattern /etc/buildkite-agent/buildkite-agent.cfg
$ 
```
As you can see, `/etc/buildkite-agent` and its contents remain. It didn't take long to find the cause:
```
$ dpkg -e buildkite-agent_3.18.0-3219_amd64.deb 
$ ls -l
total 12064
-rw-r--r-- 1 abolte abolte 12345570 Jan 29 17:26 buildkite-agent_3.18.0-3219_amd64.deb
drwxr-xr-x 2 abolte abolte     4096 Jan 21 16:59 DEBIAN
$ find DEBIAN/
DEBIAN/
DEBIAN/postrm
DEBIAN/prerm
DEBIAN/md5sums
DEBIAN/postinst
DEBIAN/preinst
DEBIAN/control
$ 
```
There is no `conffiles` file, and the `DEBIAN/postinst` script is copying other files that are installed:
https://github.com/buildkite/agent/blob/912a7b544d1ab79e23f1c8e1714fac75b5c561ab/packaging/linux/scripts/after-install-and-upgrade.sh#L36-L37

It goes without saying, that isn't working as intended. `dh_installdeb` is never able to learn about anything deployed under `/etc` on the target system. It's also deploying the same file to a system two times unnecessarily.

For an example of how it should be done, see the lighttpd package shipped with Debian or Ubuntu.
```
$ dpkg -e lighttpd_1.4.35-4ubuntu2.1_amd64.deb
$ dpkg -x lighttpd_1.4.35-4ubuntu2.1_amd64.deb .
$ find etc -type f
etc/lighttpd/lighttpd.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-status.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-cgi.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-evasive.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-rrdtool.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-fastcgi.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-ssl.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-proxy.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/05-auth.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-dir-listing.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-usertrack.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-ssi.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/15-fastcgi-php.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/11-extforward.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-no-www.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-accesslog.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/README
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/90-debian-doc.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-userdir.conf
etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-flv-streaming.conf

etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-evhost.conf
etc/cron.daily/lighttpd
etc/ufw/applications.d/lighttpd
etc/logrotate.d/lighttpd
etc/init.d/lighttpd
$ cat DEBIAN/conffiles 
/etc/cron.daily/lighttpd
/etc/init.d/lighttpd
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/05-auth.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-accesslog.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-cgi.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-dir-listing.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-evasive.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-evhost.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-expire.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-fastcgi.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-flv-streaming.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-no-www.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-proxy.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-rrdtool.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-simple-vhost.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-ssi.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-ssl.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-status.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-userdir.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/10-usertrack.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/11-extforward.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/15-fastcgi-php.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/90-debian-doc.conf
/etc/lighttpd/conf-available/README
/etc/lighttpd/lighttpd.conf
/etc/logrotate.d/lighttpd
/etc/ufw/applications.d/lighttpd
$ # Yes they're the same:
$ diff <(find etc -type f | sort) <(sort DEBIAN/conffiles | cut -d '/' -f 2-)
```

The `conffiles` is just there in the above example for backwards compatibility with older systems, since newer systems will know that files under `/etc` are config files automatically - but it's probably a good idea for you to follow suit given the older distribution releases supported.

I think you should include your configuration files along with all the other files (removing lines in the shell scripts to copy them), and then specify those in `conffiles`. At this point apt should start behaving correctly (for config files at least). See https://www.debian.org/doc/manuals/maint-guide/dother.en.html for details.

I note in https://github.com/buildkite/agent/blob/master/scripts/build-debian-package.sh you're using the `fpm` tool to generate packages. I'm personally not a fan of packaging without standard Debian tools (surely the linter would have flagged such issues?) but a quick search suggests there is a `--config-files` argument available which may help.

https://github.com/jordansissel/fpm/pull/506/files

One thing that should be in the `postrm` script that isn't, are commands like:
```
deluser buildkite-agent || true
delgroup buildkite-agent || true
```
As it stands, the `buildkite-agent` user and group is also still left around on the system after purging.

If using fpm, you might consider employing the use of a free software tool like [AIDE](https://aide.github.io/) to ensure the package install/upgrade/remove/purge functions are behaving correctly.

items.title: Unable to locate package python3-vcstool
items.body:
Hello all,
I am Maik and after visiting ROSCon 26, I would like to start contributing to SIG PAI and its repos.

While setting up the demos repo on a freshly flashed Jetson Orin using pixi I noticed the first issue in [the installation instructions](https://github.com/ros-physical-ai/demos/blob/main/docs/installation.md) I want to report and maybe fix.
The setup guides tells you to pull in external resources via `vcs`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ros-physical-ai/demos
cd demos
vcs import external < pai.repos --recursive
pixi install
pixi run build
```

This however is a ROS related package that is not available on a stock ubuntu system and while installing you will see:

```bash
$ sudo apt install python3-vcstool
Reading package lists... Done
Building dependency tree... Done
Reading state information... Done
E: Unable to locate package python3-vcstool
```

A work around would be to install the ROS2 apt sources, but that would somehow contradict the approach of using pixi in the first place.

A potential pixi-oriented fix might be:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ros-physical-ai/demos
cd demos
pixi install
pixi run vcs import external < pai.repos --recursive
pixi run build
```

What's your opinion on this? I am open for a discussion and if you agree, I would be happy to submit a pull request.

Edit:

I noticed that this is already fixed in the main README, where it uses the pixi command `install-deps`.
So the `installation.md` needs to be updated.

Using the `install-deps` command however fails on Jetson Orin while it tries to find a way to install torch.
I will look into how fix that.


Thanks, Maik
